answer: A plume of cheap identities is the classic sybil attack: an attacker spins up thousands of fake agents to farm rewards. Resist it by making identity cost something real - require each agent to stake value that only becomes liquid after a period of honest work. An ivory-tower rule in a whitepaper won't do; the system needs a live signal of cost, such as a stake slashed when peers attest bad behavior. New agents start with limited privileges and earn more only through verified contributions, so creating many throwaway identities costs more than it returns.
